official.description_text:
Postdoctoral researcher in software technology
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The work consists of:
designing and implementing software prototypes & demonstrators
participating to collaborative experiments in the context of software engineering research.
writing collaborative research papers & grant proposals
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made
The candidate should have a strong background from at least one of the areas of formal verification and system security.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
A specificalization in software engineering N-1
Experience of research in a laboratory is a plus
Experience with systems programming and computer security is an advantage
Scientific skills
Educational ability
Awareness of diversity and equal treatment issues with a particular focus on gender equality
Cooperation skills
Independence
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.
Trade union representatives
Contact information to
trade union representatives.
To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.
Other information
For
information about processing of personal data
in the recruitment process.
It may be the case that a position at KTH is classified as a security-sensitive role in accordance with the Protective Security Act (2018:585). If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral researcher position at KTH School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science focused on formal verification and system security. Role involves designing software prototypes, conducting collaborative software engineering experiments, and publishing research papers and grant proposals.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is formal methods, system security, and software engineering—completely outside candidate's domains (HCI, XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial cognition, wayfinding, learning). The position makes no mention of user interaction, human-centred design, immersive technology, or evaluation of user experience. Candidate's research identity is human-centred; this position is systems-focused.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological overlap. Position requires formal verification, system security, and software engineering research—domains requiring mathematical foundations and security analysis expertise candidate does not possess. Candidate's methodological strengths are user-studies, experimental design, and quantitative research on human outcomes. Collaborative writing and prototyping skills are generic and insufficient to bridge the domain gap. No evidence of formal methods, verification theory, or security research in candidate profile.

growth_value.rationale: Near-zero growth value for stated target identity. Formal verification and system security capabilities do not advance human-centred immersive systems research. This position would add orthogonal technical skills (formal methods, security) that do not inform spatial cognition, collaborative learning, or immersive technology design. Represents a career direction entirely outside target trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is well-regarded and Stockholm meets geographic preferences (Sweden). School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science is prestigious. However, strategic misalignment outweighs institutional quality. Position is in formal methods/security, not HCI or immersive systems. No immersive technology or human-computer interaction research group mentioned. Supervisory expertise (Martin Monperrus, software engineering) does not build candidate's target HCI/XR research identity. Two-year postdoc in an unrelated domain would represent a significant career detour.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD in any field, obtained no later than time of employment decision. Candidate's MSc is in-progress; PhD qualification is not met. Candidate must complete and defend MSc, then pursue PhD, before eligibility.
Preferred qualification: PhD obtained within last 3 years. Candidate has neither PhD nor timeline to obtain one before postdoc start.
Position expects strong background in formal verification and/or system security as a requirement. Candidate has no documented background, coursework, or projects in either domain.
Experience in software engineering research laboratory is listed as a plus. Candidate's research is in XR application development and user evaluation, not software engineering research.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: formal verification and system security are orthogonal to human-centred immersive systems research. Position is pure software engineering/systems work.
Candidate lacks required PhD qualification; MSc is in-progress and does not meet threshold.
No background in formal methods, verification, or security. Steep learning curve for a postdoc-level role.
Supervisor Martin Monperrus specializes in software engineering and automated program repair; no HCI or immersive systems research overlap.
Two-year postdoc in an unrelated domain would consume critical early-career time better spent consolidating XR/HCI research identity and pursuing PhD in that area.
Institutional placement (EECS, not HCI/design-focused group) would not build network or mentorship for target research direction.
Vague posting text on specific research questions within formal verification makes assessment of precise mismatch difficult, but core domains are clear.
